comments.author: @GaryWatts-f2c
comments.text: My wife and I have been married over 50 years and we are now over 80 yo. We have two vehicles. A 1996 Buick Regal with over 202,000 miles and a 1998 Chevy S10 truck with over 167,000 miles. Both have small problems, mostly cosmetic, but they should last as long as we do. But, I have noticed dealer inventory for new and especially used cars has been rising every time you pass the dealership. Some of the medium sized used dealers who had 50 to 70 cars 18 months ago now have 125 to 200 cars on their very over crowed lot. All of them have to be floor planned by some bank and it is only a matter of time till they can not afford to do so. The used car dealer is getting deals he can not turn down thinking the profit awaits just down the road. I believe a lot of these deals are leases coming back to new car dealers. But people like me (and there are millions of us) are not going to buy any car unless we (like the dealer) get a deal we can not turn down. Sales are down now partly because people have been financing the car for 6 or 7 or maybe 8 years which takes them out of the market for 6 or 7 or 8 years or longer. I think the entire lease program is having a negative effect. There are probably many negative things effecting the market including new car gas mileage, cost of new cars, etc.  When I was young my dad was in the car business and had his own used car dealership and had several friends with used car businesses. He worked for several new car dealers at times. During this time (late 50s, 60s and early 70s) people traded new cars every 3 or 4 years. Most of the time a new car got financed for 3 years. Some folks would keep a car 4 years so they would have 1 year without a payment.  My first car was a 5 yo Chevy which cost $1,100.00. The total cost now to purchase and maintain a vehicle is staggering. But the manufacturers are still producing more than they need and this is filtered down to used dealers but they do not pass the savings on to us consumers. IF they did an 80 yo consumer might go out on a limb and buy something. I do not expect them to do so until it is to late for the whole industry. It is only the opinion of an old man but I think the entire automobile industry will see a serious failure before  another 12 months (June 27). THEN we will find a good deal from the bank that repo's the cars.
